correctness.rationale: I inspected the assigned certificate and verifier and independently replayed the full finite classification. The construction uses \(\mathbb F_8=\mathbb F_2[z]/(z^3+z+1)\), all nine Desarguesian spread components, all 36 unordered component pairs, and all 49 nonzero normals outside each dual-spread union. For every instance the exact \(7\times95\) binary generator was formed and every message subspace was enumerated in reduced row-echelon form: 127, 2667, 11811, 11811, 2667, 127, and 1 subspaces in dimensions 1 through 7, or 29,211 per code. The full 1,764-instance replay therefore checked 51,528,204 subcode supports. Every instance matched the packaged complete spectra and hierarchy \((22,56,74,84,90,93,95)\). The dimension-one spectrum exactly reproduces the source Example 1 weight enumerator, providing an external anchor on the code construction.
correctness.risk: This is an exact finite classification of one explicit Desarguesian model; it does not prove permutation equivalence of the 1,764 codes or a formula for arbitrary \(m,r\).

evidence: Chung--Jin--Kim provides complete ordinary weights and optimality of outside normals across the affine-half family.

value.rationale: Generalized Hamming weights and full subcode-support spectra are natural invariants of a linear code and matter beyond ordinary weight distributions. The result classifies those invariants for every optimal-normal instance of a concrete current construction and discovers a nontrivial isospectrality across 1,764 codes. The exact fact is not implied by the published ordinary enumerator and is plausibly useful for later equivalence, wiretap, and support-geometry analysis.
value.risk: The result is computational and finite, and it does not yet explain the common spectrum by a closed group-action theorem.

final_claim: In the explicit \(m=6,r=2\) Desarguesian affine-half construction of Chung--Jin--Kim Example 1, all \(36\cdot49=1764\) outside-normal optimal \([95,7,22]_2\) instances have generalized Hamming weights \((22,56,74,84,90,93,95)\), and in every subcode dimension \(1\) through \(7\) they share the exact complete support-size spectra printed in RESULT.md.
limitations: The conclusion is restricted to the explicit \(m=6,r=2\) Desarguesian model.
Higher-support isospectrality does not imply coordinate-permutation equivalence.
